exec_summary.bullet: **Interest rate tightening:** A net 43.8% of Slovak firms reported tighter loan interest rates, up 38.3 pp from a net 5.5% and now above the EA's net 40.0%, raising debt servicing costs.
**Margin squeeze persists:** Labour costs rose for a net 78.81% of Slovak firms, 19.85 pp above the EA, while a net 12.83% still reported declining turnover — compressing operating margins.
**Weak demand outlook:** Slovak firms' turnover expectations fell to a net 6.75%, trailing the euro area's net 25.88% by 19 pp and signalling weaker domestic demand ahead.
**Credit line stress:** The Slovak credit line gap rose to +15.3pp from +14.8pp as need outpaced near-neutral availability, leaving Slovak firms more stressed than the EA's +14.0pp.

sections.title: Changes in Terms and Conditions of Bank Financing (Q10)
sections.finding: Slovak firms reported a net 43.8% experiencing interest rate tightening in wave 39
bullets: A net 43.8% of Slovak firms (n=76) reported tighter interest rates, up 38.3 pp from 5.5% in the prior wave, now above EA (40.0%) and DE (42.5%) — raising debt servicing costs.

A net 12.4% of Slovak firms (n=74) reported smaller available loan or credit line sizes, rising 6.3 pp from the previous wave, exceeding the EA (net 9.1%) and DE (net 7.9%) — limiting liquidity buffers.
Loan maturity conditions tightened for a net 11.6% of Slovak firms (n=76), compared with a net 4.4% in the EA and net 3.4% in DE — reducing financial flexibility.

chart.chart_subtitle: Net 43.8% of Slovak firms reported interest rate tightening.

sections.title: Financing Need vs Availability Gap (Q5/Q9)
sections.finding: Credit line stress persists as Slovak firm demand outpaces bank loan easing
bullets: The Slovak credit line gap rose to +15.3pp (n=270) from +14.8pp in the previous wave, driven by rising need (+15.2pp) with availability near neutral (-0.1pp), leaving Slovak firms more stressed than the EA (+14.0pp).
The Slovak trade credit gap swung from +6.3pp to -1.7pp (n=180), as need fell from +7.1pp to -3.4pp, placing Slovak firms less stressed than the EA (+11.0pp).
The Slovak bank loan gap deepened to -6.0pp (n=214) from -4.0pp in the previous wave, driven by improved availability (+5.6pp), leaving Slovak firms less stressed than the EA (+2.8pp).

sections.title: Expected Availability of External Financing (Q23)
sections.finding: Slovak firms' bank loan availability outlook diverged from improving EA trend
bullets: A net 6.46% of Slovak firms (n=104) expected bank loan availability to worsen in wave 39, down 1.30 pp from wave 38, while the EA improved 1.45 pp to 2.35%, signalling tighter conditions ahead.
Credit line availability expectations eased by 3.16 pp to a net 3.87% of Slovak firms (n=136) expecting deterioration—compared with a net 2.25% for the EA, still pointing to cautious lender behavior.

Trade credit pessimism receded, with a net 6.18% of Slovak firms (n=90) expecting deterioration—improving by 4.04 pp from wave 38's net 10.22%, though remaining above the EA's net 1.87%, limiting supplier-backed financing options.

chart.question_caption: Do you expect financing to get easier or harder in the next few months?
chart.chart_subtitle: A net 6.46% of Slovak firms expect bank loan availability to deteriorate.

sections.title: Purpose of Financing (Q6A)
sections.finding: Slovak firms shifted toward fixed investment while working capital use remained elevated
bullets: Fixed investment citation rose from 34.2% to 40.7% among Slovak firms (n=242), a 6.5 pp increase that brought Slovakia above the euro area's 38.4% — suggesting stronger long-term growth capacity.
Inventory and working capital remained the dominant financing purpose for Slovak firms (n=242) at 57.0%, 16.2 pp above the euro area's 40.8% — highlighting persistent liquidity needs.
The share of Slovak firms (n=241) citing refinancing or paying off obligations fell from 21.5% to 17.0%, easing 4.5 pp from the previous wave.

chart.question_caption: What did your firm use financing for this quarter?
chart.chart_subtitle: 57% of Slovak firms cited working capital as financing purpose.

sections.title: Factors Affecting Access to External Financing (Q11)
sections.finding: Bank willingness to lend held steady for Slovak firms, above EA
bullets: A net 7.8% of Slovak firms (n=310) reported an improvement in banks' willingness to provide credit, unchanged from the previous wave and outpacing the EA's net 5.6% — suggesting easier financing conditions.
The general economic outlook deteriorated for a net 51.6% of Slovak firms (n=472), down 7.2 pp from the prior wave and 22.2 pp below the EA net of 29.4%, pressuring credit demand.
Access to public financial support improved for Slovak firms (n=310), with the net balance rising from -33.8% (wave 38) to -21.2% (wave 39), though conditions remained adverse.

sections.title: Business Situation Indicators (Q2)
sections.finding: Slovak turnover improved but remained negative, lagging the euro area
bullets: A net 12.83% of Slovak firms (n=242) reported declining turnover in wave 39, improving 13.39 pp from wave 38, yet still contrasting with the EA's net 8.11% increase — suggesting weaker demand.
A net 34.38% of Slovak firms (n=242) reported falling profits, improving 5.42 pp from wave 38, while the EA's net decline stood at 15.39% — a gap of around 19 pp — limiting investment capacity.
Labour cost pressures remained elevated, with a net 78.81% of Slovak firms (n=242) reporting increases — 19.85 pp above the EA net — squeezing margins further.

sections.title: Expected Changes in Turnover and Investment (Q26)
sections.finding: Slovak firms' turnover outlook fell sharply, diverging from euro area optimism
bullets: Slovak firms' turnover expectations fell to a net 6.75% (n=228), trailing the euro area's net 25.88% by 19 pp in wave 38 — signalling weaker domestic demand.
Slovak turnover expectations declined by 14 pp from a net 20.90% two waves earlier, while the euro area's outlook rose from net 23.16% to net 25.88% — highlighting a growing competitiveness gap.
Fixed investment expectations bucked the turnover trend, rising to a net 14.67% (n=228) — above the euro area's net 9.45% — up 3.88 pp from the previous wave.

sections.title: Price, Wage and Employment Expectations (Q31/Q34)
sections.finding: Slovak firms face margin compression as input costs outpace selling prices
bullets: Slovak firms (n=224) expected production input prices to rise 7.33% — versus only 3.75% for selling prices (n=222) and 5.35% across the EA, pointing to continued margin compression.
Slovak firms (n=233) anticipated 4.12% average wage growth over the next 12 months, compared with 2.60% across the EA (n=4,941), adding further cost pressure.
Twelve-month inflation expectations among Slovak firms (n=193) eased to 4.68% from 4.97% in the previous wave, remaining 0.80 pp above the EA mean of 3.88%.

chart.question_caption: How much do you expect inflation to rise or fall next year?
chart.chart_subtitle: Slovak firms expect +7.33% input price rise, vs EA's 5.35%.

sections.title: Inflation Risk Outlook (Q33)
sections.finding: Slovak firms' upside inflation risk bias widened against the euro area trend
bullets: A net 61.2% of Slovak firms (n=242) saw inflation risks skewed to the upside over five years—suggesting heightened pricing pressure expectations.
Slovakia’s net upside inflation risk balance rose from 58.9% in the previous wave to 61.2%, moving in the opposite direction to the euro area, which eased from 55.3% to 54.0%.
The SK–EA gap on long-run upside inflation risk widened from 3.6 pp to 7.2 pp across consecutive waves—indicating diverging inflation perceptions.

chart.question_caption: What’s the biggest inflation risk in five years?
chart.chart_subtitle: Slovak firms' upside inflation risk balance reached 61.2%.

sections.title: Most Pressing Business Problems (Q0B)
sections.finding: Skilled staff and production costs dominate Slovak firms' business concerns
bullets: Among the seven problems tested, skilled staff availability was the top concern for Slovak firms (n=239), scoring 6.64/10 — up 0.57 points from wave 38, exceeding the EA's 6.57/10, highlighting a growing talent gap.
Costs of production or labour ranked second at 6.62/10 (n=240), rising 0.43 points from wave 38, just below the EA score of 6.74/10, squeezing margins further.
Regulation scored 6.10/10 (n=236), easing marginally by 0.08 points from wave 38, yet remaining above the EA average of 5.87/10, still burdening compliance efforts.

chart.question_caption: How important were these problems for your firm?
chart.chart_subtitle: Skilled staff scored 6.64/10 for Slovak firms in wave 39.
